about: The field library: real, teachable sorting questions, drawn from how biology, geography and everyday life already classify things (the owner's ruling of 7 Oct 2026). For a circle with no field, the model CHOOSES questions from here that apply; it does not invent them. The four tests then decide (tools/job/fields.py). The model may propose a new question only when nothing here fits; it goes through the same tests, and if it passes it is added here with a note saying so. A question may have more than four values: a board uses any four that have enough familiar things. Where things overlap, the wording asks what is MOSTLY true. Two rules from the owner, of the night of 7 Oct 2026. Keep profundity: real, teachable distinctions only, never colour or size. And where all the things of a circle share one answer (all fish live in water, all insects have six legs), ask for the real distinction WITHIN them (where the fish mostly lives).
how_to_add: Add a question by hand under `questions`: an id of its own, the wording as said to the child, where it applies, where the classification comes from, and its values with a short group name each. `for` holds circles as the catalogue names them (python tools/catalogue/catalogue.py circles): `animal` covers every circle inside Animals, `animal/mammal` only Mammals and what is inside it. Nothing else needs changing; the next run can choose it.
